answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, natural language):

Original-study effect sizes are larger than replication-study effect sizes in ALL domains in this dataset, but the degree differs by domain. Original effects exceed replication effects in 82–88% of paired studies (Social 30/34 = 88.2%; Economics 15/18 = 83.3%; Cognitive 28/34 = 82.4%; overall 73/86 = 84.9%), and the within-pair gap (Fisher-z, d_f = fiso − fisr) is significantly positive in every discipline (paired Wilcoxon p = 1e-6 Social, p = 6e-6 Cognitive, p = 8.4e-4 Economics). What differs across domains is HOW much larger the original tends to be:

• STRONGEST in Social psychology (Psychology/RPP project, n=34) — by proportional magnitude, replications shrink to ~22% of the original effect (median |rr|/ro = 0.224, i.e., the original is ~4.5× larger), with 10 of 34 (29%) replications reversing direction; its magnitude shrinkage is significantly larger than Economics (log-ratio contrast p = 0.0033).

• INTERMEDIATE in Cognitive psychology (Psychology/RPP project, n=34) — replications retain ~67% of the original magnitude (original ~1.5× larger, median |rr|/ro = 0.671); it shows the largest median absolute Fisher-z gap (0.249) only because its original effects are the largest in absolute terms (median fiso = 0.634), not because replication is worse.

• WEAKEST / MOST FAITHFUL in Economics = Experimental Economics (ee) project (n=18) — replications retain ~70% of the original magnitude (original ~1.4× larger, median |rr|/ro = 0.698), the smallest median Fisher-z gap (0.143), and the fewest direction reversals (3/18).

RANKING summary: by magnitude shrinkage, Social ≫ Cognitive ≈ Economics; by median absolute Fisher-z gap, Cognitive ≈ Social > Economics. The signed-gap ranking is NOT statistically distinguishable across disciplines (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.54; ANOVA F(2,83)=0.28, p = 0.75); the only significant cross-domain difference is proportional magnitude shrinkage, driven by Social vs Economics (p = 0.003). 

Sign-handling: I used signed replication effects (rr), so direction-reversed replications (18/86 overall) count as smaller than the original; the magnitude interpretation (|rr|/ro) yields the same domain ranking, so the conclusion is robust to this choice. Confound: discipline and replication project are perfectly aligned — Economics = the ee project (n=18), Social+Cognitive = the Psychology/RPP project (n=68). Because Economics rests on only 18 studies, its "most faithful" rank and all conclusions are specific to the RPP and Experimental Economics replication projects and should not be over-generalized.

payload.hypothesis: Original-study effect sizes are larger than replication-study effect sizes in every domain (Social, Cognitive, Economics), with original > replication in 82-88% of paired studies and significantly positive within-domain paired gaps (all p<0.001). The degree differs by domain: strongest in Social psychology (Psychology/RPP project, n=34) where replication magnitudes shrink to ~22% of original (original ~4.5x larger; median |rr|/ro=0.224; 10/34 direction reversals; shrinkage significantly larger than Economics, p=0.003), intermediate in Cognitive psychology (Psychology/RPP project, n=34; ~1.5x larger; median |rr|/ro=0.671; largest median absolute Fisher-z gap 0.249 only because original effects are largest in absolute terms), and weakest/most faithful in Economics = Experimental Economics project (n=18; original ~1.4x larger; median |rr|/ro=0.698; smallest median Fisher-z gap 0.143; only 3/18 reversals). Ranking by magnitude shrinkage: Social >> Cognitive = Economics; by median absolute Fisher-z gap: Cognitive = Social > Economics. Cross-domain signed-gap differences are not significant (ANOVA p=0.75); only proportional magnitude shrinkage differs significantly (Social vs Economics p=0.003). Sign-handling: signed rr (reversed replications count as smaller); magnitude interpretation gives the same ranking. Confound: economics = ee project; social+cognitive = rpp/Psychology project. Caveat: Economics n=18 limits generalizability to these two replication projects.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded 86 paired studies (core ES columns complete, no duplicates). 2) Defined within-study differences d=ro-rr and d_f=fiso-fisr (verified fiso=atanh(ro), fisr=atanh(rr) exactly), and magnitude ratio |rr|/ro. 3) Built per-domain descriptive tables at discipline and project level (means/medians on both correlation and Fisher-z scales, % original>replication, median/mean gaps, magnitude ratio, # direction reversals). 4) Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank and paired t-tests within each domain on d_f and d. 5) Cross-domain comparison: Kruskal-Wallis on d_f and on log|rr|/ro, OLS of d_f ~ discipline (ref=Economics) and of log|rr|/ro ~ discipline, ANOVA, and binomial tests that %(ro>rr) exceeds 50%. 6) Produced two zero-dependency SVG plots (paired Fisher-z scatter colored by discipline with identity line; mean original vs replication bars with SE) and CSV tables. Full reproducible script: analysis/analysis_script.py.
